verses.text: Another time Jesus went into the synagogue. A man with a shrivelled hand was there.
Some people were watching Jesus closely to see if he would heal the man on the Sabbath. They wanted a reason to accuse him.
Jesus said to the man with the shrivelled hand, "Stand up here in front of everyone."
Then he asked them, "Which is allowed on the Sabbath, to do good or to do evil? To save a life or to kill?" But they said nothing.

Jesus looked around at them in anger. He was very sad because their hearts were so hard. He said to the man, "Stretch out your hand." The man stretched it out, and his hand was healed and made as good as the other.
Then the Pharisees went out and straight away began to make plans with Herod's supporters about how they could kill Jesus.
Jesus went away with his followers to the lake, and a large crowd from Galilee followed. People also came from Judea,
from Jerusalem, from Idumea, from the other side of the Jordan River and from around Tyre and Sidon. A large crowd came to him because they heard about all the things he was doing.
Because of the crowd, Jesus told his followers to have a small boat ready for him, so that the people would not crush him.
He had healed many people, so all who were sick kept pushing forward to touch him.
Whenever evil spirits saw him, they fell down in front of him and shouted, "You are the Son of God!"
But Jesus gave them strict orders not to tell anyone who he was.
Jesus went up on a mountain and called to him the men he wanted, and they came to him.
He chose twelve of them to be with him, so that he could send them out to preach.
He also gave them authority to heal sicknesses and to drive out demons.
These are the twelve he chose: Simon, whom he gave the name Peter,
James, the son of Zebedee, and his brother John. Jesus gave these two the name Boanerges, which means "Sons of Thunder".
Then there were Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James, the son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Zealot,
and Judas Iscariot, who later handed Jesus over to his enemies. Then Jesus went into a house.
Again a crowd gathered, so that Jesus and his followers could not even eat.
When his family heard about this, they went to take charge of him. They said, "He has gone mad."
The teachers of the law who came down from Jerusalem said, "He has Beelzebul in him! He drives out demons by the power of the ruler of the demons."
So Jesus called them to him and spoke to them using stories. "How can Satan drive out Satan?
If a kingdom fights against itself, that kingdom cannot last.
If a family fights against itself, that family cannot last.
And if Satan fights against himself and is divided, he cannot last. His end has come.
No one can go into a strong man's house and steal his things unless he first ties up the strong man. Then he can rob his house.
I tell you for certain, people will be forgiven all their sins and all the evil things they say against God.
But whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit will never be forgiven. They are guilty of a sin that lasts for ever."
Jesus said this because they were saying, "He has an evil spirit."
Then Jesus' mother and brothers came. They stood outside and sent someone in to call him.
A crowd was sitting around Jesus. They told him, "Your mother and brothers and sisters are outside looking for you."
"Who is my mother? Who are my brothers?" Jesus asked.
Then he looked at the people sitting in a circle around him. He said, "Here are my mother and my brothers!
Anyone who does what God wants is my brother and sister and mother."
